howTo: Enter the pitch diameter of pulley 1 (D1) and pulley 2 (D2) in millimeters (mm). Either pulley can be the driver or driven.
Enter the shaft center-to-center distance (C) in millimeters. Verify that the center distance exceeds half the sum of both pulley diameters to avoid physical pulley interference.

The tool computes the required theoretical pitch length (L) of an open belt, the contact wrap angle on the smaller pulley (β_small), and the wrap angle on the larger pulley (β_big). Use the small pulley wrap angle to check against the minimum recommended 120° wrap for adequate friction.
formula: D_big = max(D1, D2), D_small = min(D1, D2), r = (D_big − D_small)/(2C) | L ≈ 2C + (π/2)(D_big + D_small) + (D_big − D_small)² / (4C) | β_small = 180° − 2·arcsin(r) | β_big = 180° + 2·arcsin(r)

examples.title: Speed reduction drive with 2:1 pulley ratio
examples.description: Standard layout with D1 = 120 mm driver pulley, D2 = 60 mm driven pulley, and shaft center distance C = 300 mm.
notes: Theoretical pitch length is 885.74 mm. Check standard catalog sizes (e.g. 880 mm or 900 mm pitch lengths) and adjust motor take-up slot travel accordingly.
The small pulley wrap angle is 168.52°, well above the critical 120° minimum limit, ensuring reliable friction transmission without slippage.

examples.title: Equal diameter pulleys (1:1 direct transfer drive)
examples.description: A conveyor transfer drive with identical 100 mm pitch diameter pulleys at 400 mm center distance.
notes: When D1 = D2, the ratio term (D_big − D_small)² / (4C) equals zero, simplifying length to L = 2C + π·D = 800 + 314.16 = 1114.16 mm.
Both pulleys achieve a 180° contact wrap angle.

examples.title: Heavy-duty drive with large center distance (250 mm / 100 mm / 600 mm)
examples.description: Industrial drive layout with D_big = 250 mm, D_small = 100 mm, and shaft center distance C = 600 mm.
notes: Small pulley wrap angle is β_small = 180° − 2·arcsin(0.125) = 165.64°, well above the critical 120° threshold.

references.title: Shigley's Mechanical Engineering Design (Budynas & Nisbett)
references.note: Chapter on Flexible Mechanical Elements. Theoretical basis for planar two-pulley Euclidean geometry, contact wrap angle derivations, and open belt pitch length series approximation.

references.title: DIN 7753-1 (Endless narrow V-belts for mechanical engineering)
references.note: Defines standardized datum lengths (L_d), datum diameters (d_d), and center distance adjustment ranges for narrow V-belts. Used for selecting nearest preferred stock size; does not define general flat or timing belt geometries.

references.title: ISO 5296 (Synchronous belt drives — Belts)
references.note: Defines pitch codes and standard pitch lengths specifically for toothed timing belts where length must correspond to an integer tooth count (L_p = z · p_b).

references.title: Machinery's Handbook (Industrial Press)
references.note: Section on Pulleys and Belt Drives: contact angle friction limits, open belt trigonometry, and recommendation of β_small ≥ 120° for non-positive friction drives.

commonMistakes: Entering outside (tip) diameter instead of pitch (datum) diameter. V-belts ride within pulley grooves, so pitch diameter is always smaller than pulley OD.
Ignoring center distance adjustment travel for installation and tensioning. Belt drives require center distance adjustment to slip the belt over flanges without prying.
Selecting center distance too close to pulley boundaries, leading to small pulley wrap angle β < 120° which severely reduces torque capacity.
assumptions: Open belt configuration where both pulleys rotate in the same direction (not a crossed belt drive).
Both shafts are parallel and in coplanar alignment without angular or axial offset.

The calculation provides theoretical pitch length; belt manufacturing stretch, elastic deflection under preload, and profile thickness are omitted and must be verified against manufacturer catalogue tables.
